title: Set up your agent
lesson: Give the agent the creative brief, the source rules, and the approval points before it starts.
sample:
# Second Spring production status
Topic: the 2 a.m. thermostat negotiation
Audience: women navigating perimenopause
Assets: original bedroom and thermostat footage
Review gates: script → storyboard → rough cut
Publishing: approval required
narration: Start with the audience, the footage you can use, and who approves the work. This setup sheet keeps every later task on the same brief.

title: Find breakout videos
lesson: Compare each video with its own channel’s usual performance at a similar age.
sample:
hook,views,channel_median,view_multiple,data_source
Nighttime habits,48000,12000,4.0,illustrative example
Relatable bedroom skit,27000,9000,3.0,illustrative example
Morning routine,18000,15000,1.2,illustrative example
narration: This example video has forty eight thousand views against a twelve thousand baseline. That is four times the usual performance. Look for the pattern behind that result.

title: Build titles & thumbnails
lesson: Pair a specific title with one readable visual idea. Check that the video delivers the promise.
sample:
# Thumbnail concept A
Title: 2 A.M. Hostage Talks With My Thermostat
Image: deadpan reaction, thermostat in frame
Overlay: 2 A.M.
Check: face and clock read at phone size
Promise: the joke lands in the first shot
narration: The title sets up the thermostat gag. Use one expressive face and two short words in the thumbnail, then check that the first shot pays it off.

title: Source the best clips
lesson: Track the original source and reuse permission alongside each candidate.
sample:
clip,source,reuse_status,decision
Thermostat insert,original footage,cleared,include
Bedroom reaction,original footage,cleared,include
Creator reaction,third-party reference,unverified,hold
narration: Keep the track record with the clip. The thermostat insert is original and cleared. The third party reaction stays out of the edit until its rights are verified.

title: Edit the episode
lesson: Build the rough cut around a payoff, a quick reset, and a reaction.
sample:
00:00–00:03 · Thermostat drops. Open on the joke.
00:03–00:12 · Cut back to the bedroom.
00:12–00:22 · Water, fan, deadpan stare.
00:22–00:30 · Reaction, then end card.
narration: Start with the thermostat drop, then cut back to why she is awake. Use short inserts for the demands and hold her reaction long enough for the joke.

title: Cut vertical clips
lesson: Reframe the subject for a phone and keep captions above platform controls.
sample:
Frame: 1080 × 1920 (9:16)
Open on: thermostat dropping to 68
Crop: center the face after the insert
Captions: short phrases above the lower interface
QA: verify crop, text contrast and audio on a phone
narration: In the vertical cut, put the thermostat and reaction near the center. Break the captions into short phrases and keep them clear of the buttons.

title: Script an original video
lesson: Write the line, the shot, and the timing together so the draft can be recorded.
sample:
# Hostage Talks, 2 A.M.
0–3s · Thermostat falls from 74 to 68.
VO: “The thermostat blinked first.”
3–12s · Bedroom. Throw off the blanket.
12–22s · Water, fan, slow breath, deadpan stare.
22–30s · Reaction and end card.
narration: The thermostat blinked first. That is the hook. Put the shot and the line side by side, then leave enough time for the deadpan reaction.

title: Produce a batch
lesson: Make related videos with different hooks and formats while keeping the same brand voice.
sample:
Second Spring · Thermostat negotiations · Skit · 30s · 9:16
Second Spring · Bedside comfort routine · Explainer · 45s · 9:16
Second Spring · A calmer evening · Branded motion · 15s · 1:1

Review each script and shot list before export.
narration: One brand, three different briefs. A comedy skit, an explainer, and a square motion piece. Each has its own script approval, then you can export them together.
beats: Give each video its own brief
